entities.summary:
Rodrigo Sánchez de Arévalo was a Spanish churchman, historian, and political theorist who played a crucial role in shaping the intellectual landscape of 15th-century Spain.

Born in the late 15th century, Arévalo was educated in the liberal arts and later pursued a career in the church, serving as a canon in the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela. He was appointed as the Bishop of Lugo in 1461, a position he held until his death in 1470.

Arévalo was a prolific writer and produced several works on theology, philosophy, and politics. His most notable work, 'De la Nobilitate Dei' (On the Nobility of God), explored the nature of God's sovereignty and the role of human beings in the divine plan. This treatise was influential in shaping the intellectual debates of the time and contributed to the development of the Spanish Inquisition.

In addition to his theological writings, Arévalo was also a skilled politician and played a key role in the governance of the Kingdom of Spain. He was a strong advocate for the interests of the clergy and worked closely with the monarchs of the time to promote the church's influence.

Despite his significant contributions to Spanish intellectual life, Arévalo's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of other historical figures. Nevertheless, his works continue to be studied by scholars today, offering valuable insights into the complex theological and political debates of the 15th century.

This 1470 death led to him being succeeded by Juan de Aranda, who became the Bishop of Lugo. The exact date of his death is October 13, 1470.

entities.summary: Rodrigo Sánchez de Arévalo was a Spanish churchman, historian and political theorist, born in 1404 in Santa María la Real de Nieva and died in 1470. He was a key figure in the development of Spanish humanism and played a significant role in the early stages of the Spanish Inquisition. His most notable work is the 'Summa de leyes', a comprehensive treatise on Spanish law and governance. This work had a profound impact on the development of Spanish institutions and the legal framework of the Spanish Empire. The 'Summa de leyes' was widely read and studied by scholars and policymakers, and its influence can still be seen in modern Spanish law. Rodrigo Sánchez de Arévalo's legacy extends beyond his own work, as he helped shape the intellectual and cultural landscape of 15th-century Spain. He was a leading figure in the debate over the role of the church in politics, and his writings on this topic continue to be studied by historians today.
